slides.say: A, B and C represent digits. Given: B C A, plus B C, is equal to A A A. C is equal to what?
We add the three-digit number B C A to the two-digit number B C, and get A A A. We only need C. Use the four steps. First write the addition vertically, lining up the ones digits on the right.

Can the leftmost digit help? A three-digit number plus a two-digit number gives a three-digit sum here. There is no new digit on the left. So we cannot use the rule that a new leading digit must be one.

Now check the ones column. The ones digits we add are A and C, and the result ends in A. So A plus C must end in A again. Nothing carries into this column. The only single digit we can add without changing the last digit is zero. So C is zero. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer
